title: Focus-Lane Cadence and Rapid Scope Eviction Playbook
creator: Ariana Kapoor
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures a lightweight, operational playbook for running a two-week focus-lane cadence and an associated rapid-scope-eviction protocol. The goal is to give product teams a repeatable, low-friction way to allocate critical-headroom staffing to a small set of high-impact items while creating clear, psychological-safe mechanisms to evict non-essential scope mid-cycle. This reduces mid-cycle firefighting, improves predictability of deliverables, and limits staff carryover that compounds into the next cycle.

Why now:
- We see repeated scope creep across multiple initiatives causing mid-cycle staff rebalancing and missed OKR commitments.
- Dedicated capacity customers and Dedicated ops require faster, more predictable rollouts with minimal context-switching.

Scope of playbook:
- Triage rules for establishing a Focus Lane (max 3 items per team per cycle).
- Decision thresholds and owner-driven eviction criteria.
- Staffing guardrails (max fraction of team allocated, on-call interactions).
- Communication templates for rapid eviction and reallocation.
- Metrics and dashboards to evaluate pilot success.

Mechanics / Decision flow (high-level):
1) Pre-cycle planning (Day -2): PMs nominate up to 3 focus-lane items with supporting metrics (user impact, cost delta, latency/SLO risk, customer requests). Each nomination includes an explicit rollback condition and an early-warning test (e.g., end-to-end smoke fails, perf regressions >15% token latency).
2) Leadership sign-off (Day -1): Product lead + Eng TL approve one "primary" focus item and optional secondary backup items. Approval includes committed headcount fraction and code-freeze windows (if applicable).
3) Week 1 checkpoint (mid-cycle): Quantitative check against two signals: engineering throughput (story points completed vs. expected) and health signals (SLOs, infra error rate). If either signal breaks pre-agreed boundaries, eviction protocol is triggered.
4) Rapid eviction (decision window = 24 hours): Owner (assignee) opens eviction notice in Linear, posts short rationale, and proposes immediate mitigations or a FAST-TRIAGE (3-person) review. If no mitigations pass, the item is demoted to Stretch and the freed staffing is reallocated to critical-path blockers.
5) Reassignment & follow-up: Reassignment instructions and rollback/compensating tasks are recorded as child issues, with automated updates to the cycle dashboard and AM/PM notification.

Staffing guardrails:
- Max 30% of a cross-functional team's engineering capacity can be dedicated to Focus Lane at any time.
- No more than two concurrent focused items requiring cross-team coordination.
- If >2 senior engineers are needed, require a cross-team headcount waiver from the product director.

Eviction criteria (examples):
- Technical: KV cache regression >12% P99 latency, or CI failures blocking merge for >48 hours.
- Business: Customer revenue impact turned out to be <25% of predicted delta after quick telemetry check.
- Operational: Post-deploy error budget burn >10% in the first 24h after staging deploy.

Communication templates (short forms used in Linear/comments):
- Eviction notice subject: [Eviction][PM-<key>] <short reason>
- Body: 1) Signal(s) that failed, 2) mitigation attempted (2-line), 3) recommended next state (Stretch/Backlog/Defer), 4) reallocation request (who to pull).

Runbook automations & dashboards:
- Dashboard widgets: Focus-Lane burn-down, SLO delta, cross-team blocker count, headcount delta, average time-to-evict.
- GitHub PR naming convention for focus-lane work: focus/PM-<key>/short-desc to enable quick filtering. Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823
- Confluence playbook doc (living): https://docs.redwood.ai/playbooks/focus-lane-2026

Pilot plan & success criteria:
- Pilot with Search & Runtime teams for two cycles (2026-W10, 2026-W11).
- Success metrics: Reduction in mid-cycle scope additions by 40%, carryover reduced by 30%, maintain SLOs with <5% extra error budget usage.

Trade-offs considered:
- Risk: Hard evictions might harm morale if not communicated empathetically. Mitigation: require a short "debrief" with the ticket owner within 3 working days.
- Risk: Over-restricting scope could slow discovery. Mitigation: keep 1 discovery slot per team outside Focus Lane and allow re-proposals.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- How to handle cross-team dependencies where eviction of upstream scope creates downstream blockers? Proposal: require a dependency map at nomination.
- Are we comfortable with automated Linear status transitions from eviction decisions? (engineering prefers manual at first).

Links & artifacts:
- Proposed dashboard mock: https://looker.redwood.ai/dashboards/focus_lane_mock
- Example PR for automation starters: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/pull/120
- Playbook draft (Confluence): https://docs.redwood.ai/playbooks/focus-lane-2026/draft

- [ED] Build Looker prototype widget and attach to pilot workspace (owner: Elena Voss) — due 2026-03-22.
